holidays.name: National Sangria Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass of fruity wine punch loaded with chopped fruit, a splash of brandy, and a lot of cheer. It is a handy excuse to turn leftover fruit and a bottle of red into a party in a pitcher.
holidays.origin: Sangria is rooted in Spain and Portugal, where fruit-infused wine drinks have been enjoyed for centuries. The name comes from the Spanish word 'sangre,' meaning blood, for its deep red color. The drink was introduced to a wide American audience at the 1964 New York World's Fair.
holidays.funFact: Under European Union rules, only sangria made in Spain and Portugal can carry the name on the label. Sangria made elsewhere has to be labeled 'aromatised wine-based drink.'

holidays.name: Underdog Day
holidays.description: A day to cheer for the long shots, the little guys, and anyone who is counted out before the game even starts. It is also a nod to the lovable cartoon superhero dog who was always humble and rhymed while saving the day.
holidays.origin: The observance honors the 1960s animated series 'Underdog,' which debuted in 1964. Its hero was Shoeshine Boy, a mild-mannered canine who turned into the caped crusader Underdog, and who spoke almost entirely in rhyme.
holidays.funFact: Underdog became a giant balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, first appearing in 1965 and returning for several years.

holidays.name: Ugly Christmas Sweater Day (Observed Around This Date)
holidays.description: A day when people proudly pull on the gaudiest, most tinsel-covered, light-up, jingle-bell-festooned knitwear they can find. The uglier the sweater, the greater the glory. Offices, schools, and parties hold contests to crown the worst offender.
holidays.origin: Holiday sweaters grew popular in the 1980s, when TV personalities like Andy Williams and Bill Cosby wore festive knits. The ironic ugly sweater party started in Vancouver, Canada, in 2001, and the trend spread worldwide. The official day is usually set for the third Friday of December, which often falls near this date.
holidays.funFact: Some ugly sweaters now come with working LED lights, built-in speakers that play carols, and even tiny pom-pom reindeer noses that stick out.

holidays.name: International Human Solidarity Day
holidays.description: A day to remember that people around the world are united by shared humanity. It encourages cooperation, generosity, and unity, and promotes the idea that diversity is strength.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly established it in 2005 to celebrate unity in diversity and to promote efforts to fight poverty. It grew out of the idea that solidarity is a fundamental value of international relations.
holidays.funFact: The day also reminds governments to honor their commitments to international agreements, and it was linked to the creation of the World Solidarity Fund to fight poverty.

holidays.name: Go Caroling Day
holidays.description: A day to bundle up, gather friends, and belt out holiday songs on neighbors' doorsteps, with or without much musical talent. Enthusiasm counts more than pitch, and cocoa is traditionally welcome afterward.
holidays.origin: Caroling traces back to medieval England, where 'wassailing' meant singing to bring good harvests and health in exchange for food and drink. Over the centuries it shifted into the Christmas carol tradition known today.
holidays.funFact: The word 'carol' originally referred to a dance accompanied by singing, not just the singing alone.
